_header.what: Machine-readable eligibility rules for each scheme, with the sample student's match result and the reasoning behind it. Draft: nothing here is verified yet.
_header.owner: Aman Kumar. Commit this file to team/aman/eligibility-rules.json from your own git account, after you verify it.
_header.lookout_feature: Stage 3 persona ranker (server/src/rank/rules.js reads criteria[] and evaluates them against the profile) and Stage 4 plan screen (the 'why you match' line is matches_persona.why_you_match). Same ids as team/aman/application-kits.json and EVENT_SCHEMA Opportunity.id.
_header.how_this_draft_was_made: Prepared for the team on 2026-10-24 from live TinyFish Fetch/Search reads of the pages cited in each criterion (plus docs/RECON_FINDINGS.md). The persona does not state family income, marks, attendance or institute, so criteria on those come out 'unknown' and the scheme becomes 'conditional'. That is intended.
verify_before_commit: Every criterion with clarity: 'unclear' (listed again in unclear_rules[]).
Tuition Fees to OBC (freeship): the income rule. The scheme page states none.
Shahu Fee Reimbursement: the category rule comes from the Overview text, not the Eligibility list.
JSW UDAAN (Vidyasaarathi): read from a search snippet only; open the scheme page.

rule.title: exact scheme name
rule.source_url: main page the rule set was read from
rule.scheme_type: Merit | Welfare | null (NSP: a student may take only ONE merit scheme, see global_rules)
rule.conflicts_with: array of { id, reason, from, read_on }: schemes that cannot be taken together
rule.verified: boolean. true only after the owner checked every criterion on the official page
rule.needs_verification: boolean. true if any criterion needs it

criterion.field: social_category | family_income_inr | course_level | course | state_domicile | gender | year_of_study | institution | admission_route | marks_percent | attendance_percent | not_other_scholarship | special_circumstance | renewal_only
criterion.value: the value compared against the persona (array for in/not_in)
criterion.persona_field: which persona key it reads, or null for 'manual'
criterion.quote: short exact phrase from the page
criterion.from: URL the criterion was read from
criterion.clarity: clear | unclear (unclear = page is ambiguous; the ranker must not hard-fail on it)
criterion.persona_check: pass | fail | unknown (unknown = persona does not state that fact)

match_result.result: match (all known criteria pass, no unknown hard rule) | conditional (no fail, some unknown) | no_match (a clear criterion fails) | unclear (outcome hinges on an unclear criterion)
match_result.why_you_match: one line, at most ~110 chars, shown on the plan screen. Lists what passed, then what is still needed.
match_result.reasoning: array of short sentences, one per decisive criterion

schema.ranker_contract: For each criterion: if persona_field is null or the persona value is null -> unknown. 'fail' only counts when clarity is 'clear'. Result = no_match if any clear fail; else unclear if any unclear criterion is decisive; else conditional if any unknown; else match. The ranker may recompute persona_check; the stored value is the author's expectation for tests.

global_rules.text: From AY 2026-27 a student may apply for one merit-based scheme and one or more welfare-based schemes on NSP.
global_rules.effect_for_persona: PM YASASVI College and PM-USP CSSS are both Merit: he can apply for only one of them.

global_rules.text: Fresh and renewal applications for AY 2026-27 will be accepted only through the MahaDBT 2.0 portal.
global_rules.effect_for_persona: Apply link is mahadbt2.maharashtra.gov.in. Deadlines are not on the 1.0 scheme pages.

tasks_for_owner: Open every 'from' URL and check each criterion's quote, value and clarity. Fix anything that is wrong.

Resolve every item in unclear_rules[]: find an official statement, update clarity and value, and record the URL and read_on date. If no official statement exists, leave it 'unclear' and say so in the reasoning.
Set verified: true on a rule ONLY after you checked all its criteria yourself.
Add rules for the 2+ new schemes you add to application-kits.json (same ids).

Write 3 test personas (e.g. female B.Tech OBC Maharashtra; male B.Tech SC Karnataka; male Diploma OBC Maharashtra) and note the expected result per scheme, so Samrat can turn them into ranker unit tests.

rules.title: PM YASASVI Central Sector Scheme Of Top Class Education In College For OBC, EBC And DNT Students

criteria.quote: OBC/EBC/DNT students having total annual family income
income from all sources up to Rs. 2.50 lakh

criteria.value: notified 'Top Class' institution with slots for the course
criteria.quote: operate in all the institutions notified by the Ministry
balance slots may be offered to eligible students studying in 2nd, 3rd and 4th year
for pursuing studies beyond class XIIth

conflicts_with.reason: Both are NSP merit-based schemes; only one merit scheme per student (global_rules nsp:one-merit-scheme).

matches_persona.why_you_match: OBC + B.Tech (2nd year) · needs family income ≤ ₹2.5 lakh and a notified 'Top Class' institute
reasoning: Category OBC and UG course pass.
2nd-year students are covered only through leftover slots after 1st-year students.
Income and whether his college is notified are unknown, so the result is conditional.

rules.title: PM-USP – Central Sector Scheme Of Scholarship For College And University Students (CSSS)

criteria.value: received the fresh award in 1st year (fresh awards use the Class XII board top-20-percentile list)
criteria.quote: Students who have received fresh scholarship
gross parental/family income upto ₹ 4.5 lakh
at least 50% marks in the Annual Examination
adequate attendance of at least 75%

criteria.value: not availing other merit schemes, state scholarships, fee waiver or reimbursement
criteria.quote: Not availing benefit of any other merit scholarship schemes, State run scholarship schemes, fee waiver, reimbursement scheme

criteria.value: renewal allowed for B.Tech at graduation level?
criteria.quote: except for the students pursuing technical courses leading to degree at graduation level

conflicts_with.reason: CSSS excludes students availing a state fee reimbursement (guideline 4(iv)).
CSSS excludes students availing a state-run scholarship (guideline 4(iv)).
Only one NSP merit-based scheme per student.

matches_persona.why_you_match: Renewal only: if you won CSSS in 1st year · 50%+ marks, 75% attendance, no state fee reimbursement
reasoning: A 2nd-year student cannot apply fresh; only a renewal is possible, and only if he/she won it in 1st year (unknown).
Taking MahaDBT OBC scholarship or freeship would disqualify him (4(iv)), so the plan must make him choose.
The FAQ's line about technical degrees conflicts with guideline section 7 (which pays B.Tech in year 4): unclear, so not a hard fail.

criteria.quote: Orphan OR Either or both parents died due to Covid 19
should not be more than Rs. 8 lakh per annum

criteria.value: AICTE-approved institution and course, regular mode
criteria.quote: AICTE Approved institutions and courses at Degree/ Diploma level in regular mode
(in 1st /2nd / 3rd /4th year)

criteria.value: not a recipient of any Central/State/AICTE scholarship
criteria.quote: should NOT be Recipient of any of the Central Govt. / State Govt. / AICTE Sponsored scholarships

conflicts_with.reason: Swanath requires not receiving any State Govt. scholarship (2.0(4)).

matches_persona.why_you_match: B.Tech in an AICTE college, 2nd year OK · only if orphan/Covid loss/martyr's ward/critical-illness case, income ≤ ₹8 lakh
reasoning: Course and year pass (2nd-year degree students get up to 3 years).
The scheme exists only for four hardship categories; the persona does not state any, so it stays conditional and must be shown with that caveat.
